column1: # C files deliberately kept inside a library that already has a build.zig.
# Enforced by scripts/checks/check_zig_parallel_trees.py, so a port that
# leaves C behind has to say so here instead of leaving a parallel tree.
# A .c under a library's tests/ needs no row: C test fixtures are how the Zig
# is held to the C ABI, and they are deliberately C.

column1: # ra8_dfu is partially migrated: the polled USB-DFU host driver is Zig,
# the boot logic the bootloader runs at reset is Zig, and
# the root-of-trust verifier is Zig; four C TUs remain. The two that
# are left of the root-of-trust block (antirollback, launch) are blocked by
# white-box suites that #include the .c files, not by the shared trailer
# record; the root-of-trust audit has the reading and the porting order.

column3: USBX DFU device class bound to real MRAM through the ux_dcd_ra8_usb bridge. Its seam is the vendored USBX callback surface rather than ra8_usb_host_*, so it ports after the host side proves the pattern.

Board boot path, kept C during the board port and ported as its own slice. ra8_add_app selects these by filename out of src/boot/ (an app-local override wins), and the linker script places them; the vector table is a table of weak aliases the image overrides, and system_init runs before anything the host suites can call. Nothing in the host gates sees a section placement or a weak override, so an ARM link is the only thing that would verify a port of them.

column1: # ra8_board_ek_ra8d2 is the first PARTIALLY ported board (RA8FW-365). The board
# core went to Zig earlier (identity, LEDs, switches, the three GLCDC pin
# tables, the panel straps, xSPI and SDHI routing, the Arduino header), as did
# the dual-core descriptor, USB port routing, bringup, the VCOM console
# stream, the clock profile, the camera, ethernet, audio-USB, touch and PDM
# layers; all of that C is deleted. Everything below is the C that has NOT
# moved yet, with the reason it has not. The flip is still partial because
# the MIPI panel unit compiles beside the archive, and sources.cmake now
# reads that off the filtered source list rather than off the board .c by

column3: J32 MIPI-DSI panel bring-up, all that is left of the old comms unit after the board clock init port moved the board clock init and the VCOM console to Zig. It instantiates ra8_mipi_dsi_config_t and ra8_mipi_phy_config_t, 308 and 345 lines of type definitions with nested timing and timeout blocks, and nothing available here would catch a mirrored-layout mismatch: no host suite reads the config back, the one suite on this path drives the real HAL against fake MMIO at the register level, and only an ARM link verifies the layout. A silent mismatch mis-programs the D-PHY PLL. Ports when the structs can be read rather than mirrored, or alongside a suite that reads back what was programmed.

EK-RA8D2 timer/PWM profiles from dev (RA8FW-299, 5eda31914), merged into zig/dev by the dev sync. The GPT adapters they bind are Zig now (libs/if_ra8_gpt has no C left), and the host suite test_ra8_board_ek_ra8d2_gpt_profile passes against that archive unchanged. The profile itself stays C until the board layer ports: it fills fw_if_timer/fw_if_pwm board-channel tables the ra8_board_ek_ra8d2 Zig archive does not yet own.

Board boot path on the first PARTIALLY ported board (RA8FW-365). ra8_add_app selects these by filename out of src/boot/ (an app-local override wins, and this board carries ns_usb_handoff and secure_only profiles as well as the default), and the linker script places them; the vector table is a table of weak aliases the image overrides, and system_init runs before anything the host suites can call. tests/cmake/library_sources.cmake globs src/*.c only, so no host suite compiles src/boot at all. An ARM link is the only thing that would verify a port of them.
